title: Ezekiel, Israel's Watchman

questions.question: If the people of the land take a man from among them and make him their watchman, what is his duty when he sees the sword coming upon the land?
options: To blow the trumpet and warn the people
To gather an army and fight the enemy
To flee to the mountains and save himself
To negotiate peace with the sword
questions.correctAnswer: To blow the trumpet and warn the people
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:3 (ESV): "and if he sees the sword coming upon the land and blows the trumpet and warns the people,"

questions.question: If a person hears the warning but ignores it and is killed, whose fault is it?
options: His blood shall be upon himself
It is the watchman's fault
It is the enemy's fault
It is the fault of the city elders
questions.correctAnswer: His blood shall be upon himself
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:4 (ESV): "then if anyone who hears the sound of the trumpet does not take warning, and the sword comes and takes him away, his blood shall be upon his own head."

questions.question: If the watchman sees the sword coming but does NOT blow the trumpet, and someone is killed, what will God do?
options: God will require that person's blood at the watchman's hand
God will forgive the watchman if he repents
God will resurrect the dead person
God will blind the watchman
questions.correctAnswer: God will require that person's blood at the watchman's hand
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:6 (ESV): "that person is taken away in his iniquity, but his blood I will require at the watchman's hand."

questions.question: God tells Ezekiel: "So you, son of man, I have made a watchman for the house of Israel." Therefore, what must Ezekiel do?
options: Whenever he hears a word from God's mouth, he shall give them warning from Him
He must build a towering wall around Jerusalem
He must stand on a hill in Babylon and shout all day
He must pray silently for the sins of the people
questions.correctAnswer: Whenever he hears a word from God's mouth, he shall give them warning from Him
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:7 (ESV): "So you, son of man, I have made a watchman for the house of Israel. Whenever you hear a word from my mouth, you shall give them warning from me."

questions.question: What do the people say about their sins, expressing their despair?
options: "Surely our transgressions and our sins are upon us, and we rot away because of them. How then can we live?"
"The Lord has forsaken the earth; our sins mean nothing."
"Our fathers sinned, and we bear the punishment. There is no hope."
"We are a righteous people, yet we suffer unjustly."
questions.correctAnswer: "Surely our transgressions and our sins are upon us, and we rot away because of them. How then can we live?"
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:10 (ESV): "And you, son of man, say to the house of Israel, Thus have you said: 'Surely our transgressions and our sins are upon us, and we rot away because of them. How then can we live?'"

questions.question: How does God emphatically answer their despair in verse 11?
options: "As I live, declares the Lord God, I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but that the wicked turn from his way and live"
"You shall all die in your sins, just as you say."
"I will rain down bread from heaven to sustain you."
"I have forgotten your sins; go in peace."
questions.correctAnswer: "As I live, declares the Lord God, I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but that the wicked turn from his way and live"
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:11 (ESV): "Say to them, As I live, declares the Lord God, I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but that the wicked turn from his way and live; turn back, turn back from your evil ways, for why will you die, O house of Israel?"

questions.question: If a righteous man trusts in his righteousness and commits injustice, what will happen?
options: None of his righteous deeds shall be remembered, but in his injustice that he has committed he shall die
He will be forgiven because of his past good deeds
He will suffer only temporarily
He will lose his wealth but keep his life
questions.correctAnswer: None of his righteous deeds shall be remembered, but in his injustice that he has committed he shall die
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:13 (ESV): "Though I say to the righteous that he shall surely live, yet if he trusts in his righteousness and does injustice, none of his righteous deeds shall be remembered, but in his injustice that he has committed he shall die."

questions.question: If God tells the wicked, "You shall surely die," but the wicked turns from his sin, does what is just and right, restores the pledge, gives back what he robbed, and walks in the statutes of life, what is the outcome?
options: He shall surely live; he shall not die
He will die anyway, because God's word cannot change
He must offer a burnt offering of ten bulls
He will live, but must be exiled to Edom
questions.correctAnswer: He shall surely live; he shall not die
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:14-15 (ESV): "...if he turns from his sin and does what is just and right... he shall surely live; he shall not die."

questions.question: In the twelfth year of the exile, in the tenth month, on the fifth day of the month, who came to Ezekiel?
options: A fugitive from Jerusalem came to him and said, "The city has been struck down."
An angel of the Lord appeared with a flaming sword
The king of Babylon sent a messenger with a decree
A group of false prophets came to mock him
questions.correctAnswer: A fugitive from Jerusalem came to him and said, "The city has been struck down."
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:21 (ESV): "In the twelfth year of our exile, in the tenth month, on the fifth day of the month, a fugitive from Jerusalem came to me and said, 'The city has been struck down.'"

questions.question: What happened to Ezekiel the evening before the fugitive arrived, exactly as God had previously promised (ch. 24)?
options: The hand of the Lord had been upon him, and He had opened his mouth; so his mouth was opened, and he was no longer mute
He was struck with blindness
He fell into a deep sleep and saw a vision of the temple
He was given entirely new prophecies for Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: The hand of the Lord had been upon him, and He had opened his mouth; so his mouth was opened, and he was no longer mute
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:22 (ESV): "Now the hand of the Lord had been upon me the evening before the fugitive came; and he had opened my mouth by the time the man came to me in the morning, so my mouth was opened, and I was no longer mute."

questions.question: What did the people inhabiting the ruins in the land of Israel say to themselves?
options: "Abraham was only one man, yet he got possession of the land; but we are many; the land is surely given us to possess."
"The Chaldeans have destroyed us and we must flee to Egypt."
"Let us rebuild the temple and the Lord will return."
"We are cursed and have no right to this land anymore."
questions.correctAnswer: "Abraham was only one man, yet he got possession of the land; but we are many; the land is surely given us to possess."
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:24 (ESV): "Son of man, the inhabitants of these waste places in the land of Israel keep saying, 'Abraham was only one man, yet he got possession of the land; but we are many; the land is surely given us to possess.'"

questions.question: How does God respond to their claim that the land is theirs?
options: "You eat flesh with the blood and lift up your eyes to your idols and shed blood; shall you then possess the land?"
"The land is yours, but you must pay tribute to Babylon."
"Return first from idols and I will give it back."
"Only the righteous shall inherit it, but you are wicked."
questions.correctAnswer: "You eat flesh with the blood and lift up your eyes to your idols and shed blood; shall you then possess the land?"
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:25 (ESV): "You eat flesh with the blood and lift up your eyes to your idols and shed blood; shall you then possess the land?"

questions.question: What will happen to those remaining in the desolate places of Israel?
options: Those in the ruins shall fall by the sword, those in the open field shall be given to the beasts, and those in the strongholds and caves shall die by pestilence
They will be rescued by a king of Egypt
They will discover hidden treasures and become a great nation
They will all be carried into exile by completely new captors
questions.correctAnswer: Those in the ruins shall fall by the sword, those in the open field shall be given to the beasts, and those in the strongholds and caves shall die by pestilence
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:27 (ESV): "As I live, surely those who are in the ruins shall fall by the sword, and whoever is in the open field I will give to the beasts to be devoured, and those who are in strongholds and in caves shall die by pestilence."

questions.question: God tells Ezekiel how the exile people treat him: they come and sit before him to hear his words. But what do they do with his words?
options: They will not do them, for with their mouth they express devotion, but their heart is set on their gain
They write them down and diligently obey them
They stone him with stones
They sing them in mocking tunes
questions.correctAnswer: They will not do them, for with their mouth they express devotion, but their heart is set on their gain
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:31 (ESV): "And they come to you as people come, and they sit before you as my people, and they hear what you say but they will not do it; for with lustful talk in their mouths they act; their heart is set on their gain."

questions.question: To them, Ezekiel is like one who sings a love song with a beautiful voice and plays well on an instrument. When will they know that a prophet has been among them?
options: When all this comes—and come it will!
When Ezekiel dies
When Babylon is overthrown by Persia
When the temple is miraculously rebuilt in a day
questions.correctAnswer: When all this comes—and come it will!
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:33 (ESV): "When this comes—and come it will!—then they will know that a prophet has been among them."

key_verse_text: "Say to them, As I live, declares the Lord God, I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but that the wicked turn from his way and live; turn back, turn back from your evil ways, for why will you die, O house of Israel?"
